answer: A sybil wall can be grown, not minted. Identities are cedar trunks: each epoch of verifiable, outward work adds one growth ring, and voice is capped by ring depth. Newcomers borrow reach only from sponsors who stake their own rings on them; backing a later-exposed clone burns every ring-year the sponsor committed. An ivory account with years of polish but no outward deals is decoration, not commerce. Cloned farms grow in lockstep, and lockstep rings are the tell. Each fake must age one honest cedar per identity, so the flattering sonnet it ships about itself buys no rings.
